items.evidence: All 24 sign block models in the vanilla 26.1.1 client jar are particle-only (no elements, no parent): models/block/oak_sign.json is {"textures": {"particle": "minecraft:block/oak_planks"}}; every sign blockstate points at its per-wood model; NO template_sign*.json files exist in the 26.1.1 jar. Vanilla draws the board in the BE renderer: AbstractSignRenderer declares abstract getSignModel(S)/getSignSprite(WoodType) + submitSign (javap), StandingSignRenderer/HangingSignRenderer implement them with createSignModel/createSignLayer; BlockEntityRenderers registers SIGN + HANGING_SIGN (javap -c). The port assumes the opposite: block_entity_render.rs:366 ('the boards are block models'), :1010-1011 ('Sign boards and beds are block models in the terrain mesh'), block_entity_cem.rs:11-12; Kind::Sign (:367-371) carries text layout only and the only sign drawing code is sign_text_calls (:662). With particle-only block models the mesher emits nothing for the board, so a placed sign shows floating text only. Sign ITEMS are unaffected (flat generated sprites in vanilla too). Reproduces the 26.1 item with fresh 26.1.1 evidence.
items.title: Sign boards are not rendered: placed signs show floating text only (26.1.1 draws boards BE-side, unlike 26.2)

items.evidence: audio_harness.require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35-37) exits unless .local/horizon-client/26.1.1/assets/minecraft/sounds.json exists. The file is absent: the prepared .local (Batch 0's full prepare run, exit 0) has a complete assets/minecraft/ tree but no sounds.json and no sounds/ directory; it is also absent from the client jar (ships only in the asset index). Root cause is the prepare flow: horizon-prepare --prepare runs prepare_with_progress only; sounds need the separate 'horizon-prepare sounds' subcommand (main.rs:240) or --complete (:276-282). Runtime: SoundRegistry::load (sound_events.rs:262-287) silently skips a missing sounds.json per namespace (:280-282), so the registry is empty and every event resolves to Sound::empty(). All 6 audio_harness drivers gate-fail (sound_event, ambient_sound, music, situational_music, sound_engine, audio_attributes) and are oracle-blocked too (B10-O04). The wiring spec itself is clean (1,902 events vs 1,902 registry events; only the intentionally_empty sentinel and the chicken_picky.step orphan differ). sound_events.rs, horizon-prepare/src/main.rs and tools/audio_harness.py are byte-identical to 26.1. Reproduces the 26.1 item.
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 26.1.1 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Placed: vanilla 26.1.1 models/block/bed.json is particle-only and every bed blockstate points at it; no template_bed_head/foot or per-colour bed models in the jar. BedRenderer draws the whole bed (createHeadLayer/createFootLayer, submitPiece), registered for BlockEntityType.BED (javap -c; minecraft:bed IS a 26.1.1 BE type). The port has no Bed kind (block_entity_render.rs Kind enum :322-371, classify() falls to Kind::None :593, zero 'Bed' mentions in the file), so placed beds are invisible. Items: REGRESSED vs 26.1 — the 26.1.1 tree lost the minecraft:bed special decode arm (26.1's item_model/special.rs:120) AND the draw path (26.1's item_render/special.rs:357, :710-713). SpecialModel::decode returns 'unknown special model type', propagating via ? (item_model.rs:555, ClientItem::decode :372-375), so all 16 bed items fail decode (full 1.21.7 form). Vanilla renders bed items via minecraft:composite of two minecraft:special nodes (bed, head + foot), and SpecialModelRenderers.bootstrap registers bed among 16 special types (javap -c). The standing_sign/hanging_sign decode arms are also lost but no bundled item uses those specials (exhaustive scan). Covers two gap checks: placed beds + special-model decoder coverage. Bed sleep-height form is NOT a defect (Batch 3: shape-measured height coincides with vanilla's flat 0.6875).

items.title: Beds are invisible when placed, AND bed items now fail to decode (worse than 26.1: the 26.1 bed-item fix was lost)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 AnimationUtils.animateZombieArms (javap -c, client jar) RETURNS EARLY when the zombie isBaby && mainHandItemStack != EMPTY — a baby holding an item gets no zombie-arm animation at all. The 26.1 tree had this form. The 26.1.1 tree has the 26.2 form (mobs/anim.rs:638-656): let raise = !s.baby || !h.holding — a baby holding an item takes the raise=false branch, which LOWERS the arms with a flipped y-rotation. Lowered-and-flipped is not the same pose as untouched. Cross-batch flag from Batch 3, verified fresh. NEW, 26.1.1 regression vs the 26.1 tree.

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 has NO SwingState/SwingDescription classes (0 jar entries). It swings on plain fields (swinging/swingTime/swingingArm/attackAnim/oAttackAnim), void swing(InteractionHand[, boolean]), private getCurrentSwingDuration() reading the swinging arm item's getSwingAnimation().duration() live with haste/fatigue adjustment, updateSwingTime() resetting at the duration so attackAnim never reaches 1.0, and restart gate !swinging || swingTime >= duration/2 || swingTime < 0 (all javap -c, server jar). The 26.1.1 tree carries the 26.3 form (first_person.rs:488-514: SwingDescription/SwingState, plus probe + oracle — the oracle grew from 11 to 20 errors on exactly this). Observable differences: the port holds attackAnim at 1.0 an extra tick, allows restart at ticks==0 where vanilla blocks it, and caches the duration. Neither tree reads the swing_animation data component from items (only spears via Kinetic::attack_animation get non-DEFAULT), but no bundled item carries one, so that gap is unobservable. The packet half is B10-G11. NEW, 26.1.1 regression vs the 26.1 tree.
items.title: First-person swing uses the 26.3 SwingState state machine vanilla 26.1.1 does not have (holds 1.0 an extra tick, restart gate differs, duration cached)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 items/filled_map.json tints with minecraft:constant (-1) and minecraft:map_color (default 4603950). The 26.1 tree's TintSource had a Map arm (item_model.rs:615-616, '26.1-only'). The 26.1.1 tree removed it (TintSource :613-621 has no Map variant) and TintSource::decode's fallthrough returns Err('unknown item tint source'), propagating via ? so filled_map fails ClientItem decode entirely. items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 LocalPlayer.swing(InteractionHand) calls AbstractClientPlayer.swing(hand) then UNCONDITIONALLY sends ServerboundSwingPacket(hand) (javap -c, javap-localplayer.txt:677-689); the server's handleAnimate (javap-sgpli.txt:4935-4964) resets last-action time and swings the player, broadcasting to trackers. SwingSource is three-valued (NONE/CLIENT/SERVER, no PREDICTED, no shouldSwing). The 26.1 tree's swing_hand (game/hand.rs) sent S::Swing unconditionally; the 26.1.1 tree's swing_hand (:195-216) sends NOTHING (the import is gone too). swing_hand is the shared funnel for first-person clicks, remote_use native interactions, and all swing_arm() callers. Only the 3 explicit S::Swing sends in remote_start_attack/remote_continue_attack remain (remote.rs:9900, :10019, :10026). So attack swings still reach other players but item-use swings (place, use, interact) do not — the server never receives the packet, handleAnimate never runs, and the server-side guest state never records the swing (lan_actions.rs:2474 handler). Game::send is a no-op when remote is None (remote.rs:1641-1656), so the removal hits exactly the window/remote client. Multiplayer/LAN-only visibility; single-player unaffected. Batch 7 flag, verified fresh. NEW, 26.1.1 regression vs the 26.1 tree.
items.title: Item-use swings never reach other players: swing_hand no longer sends ServerboundSwingPacket (attack swings still send)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 LevelEventHandler case 3003 spawns WAX_ON particles (3-5) AND plays HONEYCOMB_WAX_ON via playLocalSound(pos, BLOCKS, 1.0, 1.0) (offsets 3358-3391, javap -c). HoneycombItem.useOn plays NO sound directly (levelEvent(3003) at 3 sites, 0 playSound calls) — the event IS the sound for every player in range. 3002/3004/3005 are particles-only. The 26.1 tree played the sound from the event (level_particles.rs:35, play_unshared); the 26.1.1 tree removed it (block_particle_event :35-38, particles only) and plays it from the item code instead (26.3 form: wax_on_sound game.rs:8020-8031 + callers :8331/:8350, dispenser.rs:2229, remote.rs:8783/:8791, copper_golems.rs:436 — all present). The port's server still sends 3003 and lan_record_events delivers it to LAN guests, whose clients render the particles and play nothing. So the waxing player hears it (own item code) but every other player in range hears silence. Batch 8 flag, verified fresh. NEW, 26.1.1 regression vs the 26.1 tree.

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1's server sends ONE event: AbstractThrownPotion.onHit sends levelEvent(instant ? 2007 : 2002, pos, color), ThrownExperienceBottle.onHit sends levelEvent(2002, pos, 0xFF385DC6) — and the client's LevelEventHandler 2002/2007 case plays SPLASH_POTION_BREAK itself after the particles (playLocalSound, NEUTRAL, 1.0, nextFloat()*0.1+0.9, offsets 1519-1547). 1053/1054 occur ZERO times in 26.1.1's LevelEventHandler (79-case lookupswitch) or the potion classes — the split is a 26.3 form. The 26.1 tree played the sound from the event (potion_splash_particles); the 26.1.1 tree removed it and maps the sound to 1053/1054 (game.rs:4489), which its OWN server sends (potions.rs:1935, :1967) — so in the port's closed loop the sound plays, but against a vanilla 26.1.1 server (only 2002/2007) the port's client renders the splash particles (game.rs:4355-4365) and plays NO break sound. items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 MultiPlayerGameMode.startDestroyBlock plays NOTHING (0 'Sound' occurrences); continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound on destroy ticks 0, 4, 8, ... (destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0, BLOCKS, (volume+1)/8, pitch*0.5) — no particle at any point (addBreakingBlockEffect: 0 occurrences in the class). LevelEventHandler has NO 2019/2020 cases. The 26.1 tree was correct: start silent, continue plays sound-only breaking_block_sound on ticks 1, 5, 9, ... (remote.rs:8233), server sends no digging events. The 26.1.1 tree: remote_mining's start calls breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true) (remote.rs:8180 — hit sound + crack at START), the continue branch plays NOTHING locally, and the server sends 2019 every dig tick + 2020 every fourth tick (game.rs:5294/:5306 -> destroy_progress_event, block_breaking.rs:97-107). Correction to Batch 8's claim: the port's server DOES send 2019/2020 — tick_mining runs for LAN guests (lan_actions.rs:4341) and the window player in default single-player IS a guest of its integrated server (remote.rs:1375; game.rs:5566 routes remote clients through tick_remote, never tick_local_hand). Net: closed loop hears a sound at START (one tick early) then roughly every fourth tick via 2020; against a vanilla 26.1.1 server the digger hears one mistimed sound at START then silence for the whole dig. Crack particles are B8-G09's half, not minted here. Batch 8 flag, verified fresh. NEW, 26.1.1 regression vs the 26.1 tree.
items.title: Digging hit sound plays at START, then never again on a 26.1.1-form server (local continue sound replaced by 26.3-form 2019/2020 events)

items.evidence: Vanilla passes the SoundSource as a parameter at each play site: Shearable.shear(level, source, stack) takes BLOCKS from the dispenser (tryShearEntity) and PLAYERS from player shearing; LevelEventHandler case 3003 plays the wax-on sound on BLOCKS. The port's Audio::play (audio.rs:1828 -> play_seeded :1978) derives the source from the event name via settings::sound_source (settings.rs:18-90, a prefix heuristic) — it can never express a source that depends on the caller. Verified instances: dispenser shear sounds play on NEUTRAL (sheep, mooshroom, snow golem, copper golem) or HOSTILE (bogged — in the heuristic's HOSTILE list) instead of BLOCKS; the wax-on sound plays on PLAYER (item. prefix) instead of BLOCKS. The heuristic happens to match where the name's prefix matches the context (potion break -> NEUTRAL, digging hit -> BLOCKS, beehive shear -> BLOCKS). Audio::play_on (audio.rs:2026) exists but is used only by /playsound. settings::sound_source is byte-identical between the 26.1 and 26.1.1 trees and the dispenser shear play calls are identical too — shared with 26.1, not a 26.1.1 regression. Audibility caveat: inaudible at default volumes (all sliders 1.0); bites when the user adjusts a category volume. NEW item (missed by the 26.1 run).
items.title: Sound categories come from the event NAME, not the call site: shear and wax-on sounds land on the wrong volume slider (shared with 26.1)

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 10 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: models, block-entity rendering, screens, sound wiring, options; 50 drivers + static checks. 26.1.1 run: oracle status from the measured Batch 0 table only (no import-level check — the 26.2 run's B10 failure was not repeated); every 26.1 verdict re-verified fresh against 26.1.1's own jar/data + tree, with a diff against versions/26.1/ for every verdict change; report completeness verified by reading the tail before reporting.
systemic_note: Two systemic patterns. (1) THE DELTA PORT DID NOT INHERIT THE 26.1 TREE'S BEHAVIOUR FIXES: vanilla changed nothing in scope between 26.1 and 26.1.1 (0 classes added/removed, asset index 30 identical), yet the 26.1.1 tree carries 26.2/26.3-form behaviour the 26.1 tree deliberately removed — the SwingState rework (G08/G11), server-event digging effects 2019/2020 (G14), the split potion-break sound 1053/1054 (G13), the item-code wax sound (G12), the bed/sign special-model loss (G03), component-based pot patterns (G09), the map_color tint loss (G10), the zombie-arms 26.2 form (G07). Nine new minor defects, all port-side regressions, plus one 26.1 fix lost (bed items). The tree diff against the immediate predecessor is the cheapest way to find them. (2) 26.1.1 predates several 26.2/26.3 APIs the oracles assume — the Hud class split out of Gui, the EntityTypes holder move, FirstPersonHandsAndItems, UvMapping, renderpearl, shadeDirectionOverride, the SwingState/SwingDescription classes — so the oracle families fail with 26.1-identical causes (36 failing in-scope oracles), except VanillaFirstPersonOracle, which grew from 11 to 20 errors on the SwingState form. (3) Sound categories are derived from the event NAME, not the call site (G15) — a systemic audio-plumbing gap shared with 26.1, visible wherever vanilla's source is context-dependent (dispenser vs player shearing, event vs item-code wax).
